subject: Operational responsibility declaration request — Auriga private deployment
messages:
From: Lucia Park <lucia.park@auriga.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Auriga Platform Ops <ops@auriga.io>
Date: 2028-05-27T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: request for operational responsibility declaration

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Auriga will be moving the inference control plane into our VPC next month as discussed. Before we finalize the on-prem prep, legal and our SRE team are asking for an "operational responsibility declaration" that explicitly states which operational items remain customer-controlled and which Redwood continues to own for Private deployments.

Specifically they want clarity on:
- Network egress and NAT management (we will own NATs; want to confirm egress latency attribution)
- On-host agent upgrades (we prefer to retain admin lock for critical patches)
- Observability telemetry (what traces/logs Redwood requires vs. what we must provide)
- Fallback policy if our edge peering degrades (who triggers model fallback)

I've attached our proposed runbook (auriga_runbook_v1.pdf) and a draft responsibility matrix. Can you confirm Redwood can sign an operational declaration and indicate any evidence you will require to validate uptime/latency exclusions?

Appreciate a quick response — our go-live is slated for 2028-06-10.

Best,
Lucia
Platform & SRE Lead
Auriga Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-27T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: request for operational responsibility declaration

Team — forwarding Auriga's request. TL;DR: customer-run VPC, wants a signed operational declaration that enumerates shared responsibilities and what counts as a legitimate SLA exclusion (network egress, NAT, agent upgrades, telemetry). Go-live target 6/10.

Key asks for Legal/SRE:
- Agree on precise wording for what we will consider a customer-controlled outage (e.g., customer-configured NAT misrouting, 3rd-party transit provider degradations).
- Evidence types we accept: packet captures, BGP / peering incident receipts, SRE runbook execution logs.
- Telemetry requirements: which metrics/logs they must forward (prefix/KV cache hit rates, p95 API latency, inference error rate).

Karthik — can you draft the operational declaration language? Focus on runbook acceptance criteria and the handback trigger for model fallback. Naomi — we'll need guidance from Risk on evidence sufficiency and auditability. Vanessa — confirm whether Optimize's telemetry contractually supports the retention they propose; also estimate how this affects our observability storage.

I'll loop Legal after we have an internal draft.

-Jordan

Date: 2028-06-02T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: request for operational responsibility declaration

Lucia / Ops —

Thanks for the attachments and the clear runbook. We reviewed this with Risk and Product; below is our proposed operational responsibility declaration in principle. If this matches your expectation, we'll send the formal annex to Legal for signature.

Summary of proposed declaration (high level):
- Customer-controlled items (Auriga): NAT translation table management, customer edge egress, customer-managed transit/provider configuration, and on-host administrative changes that are initiated by Auriga SRE. These actions are considered customer-controlled and are eligible for SLA exclusion if accompanied by the evidence types below.
- Redwood-controlled items: model serving runtime, KV cache integrity, token accounting, and model fallback execution when invoked by Redwood routing policy. Redwood retains responsibility for inference code-level regressions and availability within the sandboxed runtime we deliver.

Evidence accepted for SLA exclusion: one or more of the following within the incident window — provider incident ID with timeline, runbook execution log (signed by on-call), NAT translation logs showing the window of dropped sessions, and metric traces showing sudden egress deltas. Continuous pcap files are NOT required as a default; we will accept provider incident records and filtered telemetry.

Telemetry/observability requirements:
- Auriga will expose the agreed filter of traces (request_id, path, duration) to Redwood's telemetry ingest endpoint for six weeks post-incident.
- For pre-production validation, Auriga will run the 6/6 runbook drill and share the execution log and a sample of filtered traces.

Fallback policy:
- If Auriga's edge peer experiences persistent packet loss >5% for >10 minutes (as evidenced by provider incident records and filtered traces), Redwood may automatically trigger an agreed model fallback to a hosted variant for the affected workspace. Redwood will only execute fallback after attempting the configured fallback handshake in the runbook.

Next steps:
1) Karthik / Vanessa / Naomi: please review for technical clarity and compliance risk.
2) If approved internally, I'll route the draft to Legal to produce an annex with exact clause language and signature blocks.
3) Jordan to coordinate the 6/6 runbook validation with Auriga Ops.

Notes for review: Naomi — please confirm whether the evidence bundle above suffices for audit purposes (SOC 2 evidence set). Vanessa — confirm whether the telemetry ingest window (6 weeks post-incident) is feasible without a paid observability add-on; if not, we should list a cost/plan. Karthik — please refine the fallback trigger thresholds into precise metric definitions (packet loss calculation, p95 latency deltas).

Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
